definitions.gloss: good luck, do your best, hang in there
definitions.explanation: An expression of encouragement. It comes from the verb {頑張|がんば}る (to persevere, to do one's best). Used to cheer someone on.

examples.japanese: ⟦{試験|しけん}→試験：01422_shiken⟧、{頑張|がんば}って！
{頑張|がんば}って⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦だから→だから：00924_dakara⟧、{頑張|がんば}って！
examples.english: Just a little more, hang in there!

examples.japanese: ⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{試合|しあい}→試合：01601_shiai⟧、{頑張|がんば}って⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。⟦{応援|おうえん}→応援：01900_ouen⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: Good luck in tomorrow's game. I'm cheering for you.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{疲|つか}れていた→疲れる：00901_tsukareru⟧⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧、{頑張|がんば}って⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦やり{遂|と}げました→やり遂げる：16745_yaritogeru⟧。
examples.english: He was tired from work, but he persevered and finished it to the end.

notes:
{頑張|がんば}って is the て-form of ⟦{頑張|がんば}る→頑張る：01222_ganbaru⟧ used on its own as a set expression of encouragement. It is one of the most frequently heard phrases in daily Japanese life.

WHEN IT IS USED:
- Before an exam, interview, competition, or performance
- To someone facing a difficult period (illness, heavy workload, moving house)
- As a parting phrase to someone heading into something demanding

POLITENESS LEVELS (least to most polite):
- {頑張|がんば}って: plain; friends, family, juniors
- {頑張|がんば}って⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: plain and softer, warmer
- {頑張|がんば}って⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧: polite; the safe default with strangers, colleagues, and superiors

RELATED FORMS OF THE SAME VERB:
- {頑張|がんば}れ: blunt imperative — shouted encouragement at sports events; too rough for most conversation
- {頑張|がんば}ろう: 'let's do our best' — includes the speaker, used for shared efforts
- {頑張|がんば}ります: 'I'll do my best' — the standard reply when someone says {頑張|がんば}って to you

CULTURAL NOTE: English 'good luck' appeals to chance, while {頑張|がんば}って appeals to effort and endurance — it asks the listener to keep pushing. Because of this, it can occasionally land badly on someone who is already exhausted or who cannot change their situation; ⟦{無理|むり}→無理：01558_muri⟧⟦しないで→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧ ('don't overdo it') is gentler in those cases.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ファイト→ファイト：21464_faito⟧: 'Go for it!' — casual, youthful, borrowed from English 'fight'
- ⟦{応援|おうえん}→応援：01900_ouen⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧: 'I'm rooting for you'
- ⟦うまくいく→うまくいく：21787_umakuiku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: 'I hope it goes well' — closer to English 'good luck'
